This causes attribute access like `__deepcopy__`, `__reduce__`, etc. (used by copy.deepcopy) to fall through and create new _TokenType instances instead of raising AttributeError, leading to `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable` when python's copy machinery tries to call the bogus "dunder" token type it created as if it were a method.

I'll restore the missing dunder check.

arguments.old_text:
def __getattr__(self, name):
        # don't mess with dunder
        new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
        setattr(self, name, new)
        new.parent = self
        return new
arguments.new_text:
def __getattr__(self, name):
        # don't mess with dunder
        if name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'):
            raise AttributeError
        new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
        setattr(self, name, new)
        new.parent = self
        return new

function.name: glob_files
function.description: Recursively list workspace-relative file paths that match a glob, in sorted order. The glob is matched against each file's relative path and against its file name, using Python fnmatch rules, case-sensitive: '*' and '?' also match '/', and '[abc]' matches one listed character. It never matches file contents. Cache and VCS directories (.git, __pycache__, .pytest_cache, .mypy_cache, .ruff_cache, .tox, .venv, node_modules) are skipped.

path.description: Directory (or single file) to list under, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with 1-based line numbers. start_line and end_line are inclusive; omit start_line to begin at line 1 and end_line to read to the end. The header reports the range returned and the file's total lines. Long results are shown partially with an output id for paging.

function.name: outline
function.description: List the classes and functions of a Python file with line numbers.

function.name: search_text
function.description: Search file contents for exact text (literal characters, case-sensitive; not a regex). Returns one line per match as path:line: text, with 1-based line numbers, and states the scope searched. file_glob only selects which files are searched.

query.description: Required. The exact text to find, e.g. 'def get_real_name('.

path.description: File or directory to search, relative to the workspace root. Default '.'.

file_glob.description: Optional glob selecting files by relative path or file name (same rules as glob_files), e.g. '*.py'. It never matches file contents. Default '*'.

function.name: replace_text
function.description: Replace exact text in a file. Fails without changing the file if old_text is absent, or if it occurs more than once while replace_all is false; set replace_all to replace every occurrence. Reports how many occurrences were replaced and shows the edited lines.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create a file, or overwrite it completely if it already exists, with the given content. Missing parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the workspace root.

function.name: run
function.description: Run one command in the workspace root without a shell: no pipes, redirection, chaining (&&, ;), cd, or variable expansion; use workspace-relative paths with forward slashes. 'python' and 'pytest' use the task's Python environment. Shows the command, status (including timeout), exit code, stdout, and stderr; long output is shown partially with an output id for paging. A successful exit does not mean the task is accepted.

function.name: read_output
function.description: Read part of an earlier tool result by its output id (for example out_12). Results that were shown partially say which id and range to request. Give start_line/end_line, or start_byte/end_byte for very long lines.

function.name: search_output
function.description: Find lines containing a literal string (plain text, not a regex) in an earlier tool result by its output id.

query.description: Required. The literal text to find.

function.name: history
function.description: Page through authorized durable session history. The response includes a stable next_cursor.

function.name: search_history
function.description: Find literal text in authorized prior actions and observations without knowing an output ID.

function.name: read_artifact
function.description: Read an authorized session artifact by ID, optionally using an exact byte range.

function.name: note
function.description: Save a named plain-text note that persists across turns. Pinned notes are placed in context when space allows.

function.name: read_note
function.description: Read a saved note by name.

function.name: finish
function.description: Declare the work complete. The final workspace is then checked independently.

I restored the guard clause that raises `AttributeError` for dunder names so `copy`/`deepcopy` work correctly again, while normal attribute access (e.g. `Token.Keyword`) still functions.

cli_result.result:
{"content":"The regression has been fixed. Root cause: in `sqlparse/tokens.py`, `_TokenType.__getattr__` was missing its guard for dunder attribute names (only the comment `# don't mess with dunder` remained, with no actual check). This meant accessing dunder methods like `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce__`/`__reduce_ex__` (which Python's `copy`/`copy.deepcopy` machinery probes for) would fall through to the normal logic and dynamically create a bogus new `_TokenType` instance rather than raising `AttributeError`. `copy` would then try to call that non-callable `_TokenType` object as if it were a `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce_ex__` method, producing `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable` — exactly the reported failure for 'copy issue672'.

Fix applied: restored the guard clause in `__getattr__` to raise `AttributeError` for any name that starts and ends with `__`, before creating a new token type:

```python
def __getattr__(self, name):
    # don't mess with dunder
    if name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'):
        raise AttributeError
    new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
    setattr(self, name, new)
    new.parent = self
    return new
```

Verified with a script that:

```python
    new.parent = self
    return new
```

verify_issue672.py

The regression has been fixed. Root cause: in `sqlparse/tokens.py`, `_TokenType.__getattr__` was missing its guard for dunder attribute names (only the comment `# don't mess with dunder` remained, with no actual check). This meant accessing dunder methods like `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce__`/`__reduce_ex__` (which Python's `copy`/`copy.deepcopy` machinery probes for) would fall through to the normal logic and dynamically create a bogus new `_TokenType` instance rather than raising `AttributeError`. `copy` would then try to call that non-callable `_TokenType` object as if it were a `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce_ex__` method, producing `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable` — exactly the reported failure for 'copy issue672'.

Fix applied: restored the guard clause in `__getattr__` to raise `AttributeError` for any name that starts and ends with `__`, before creating a new token type:

```python
def __getattr__(self, name):
    # don't mess with dunder
    if name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'):
        raise AttributeError
    new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
    setattr(self, name, new)
    new.parent = self
    return new
```

Verified with a script that:
- `copy.deepcopy()` on a parsed `sqlparse` statement now succeeds without error.
- `copy.deepcopy()` on a `Token` type (e.g. `Token.Keyword`) succeeds.
- Accessing `Token.__deepcopy__` correctly raises `AttributeError` instead of fabricating a bogus token.
- Normal attribute-based token creation (e.g. `Token.Keyword`, `Text.Whitespace`) still works as before.

All checks passed (exit code 0). This restores the previously-passing 'copy issue672' behaviour without affecting other functionality.

The regression has been fixed. Root cause: in `sqlparse/tokens.py`, `_TokenType.__getattr__` was missing its guard for dunder attribute names (only the comment `# don't mess with dunder` remained, with no actual check). This meant accessing dunder methods like `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce__`/`__reduce_ex__` (which Python's `copy`/`copy.deepcopy` machinery probes for) would fall through to the normal logic and dynamically create a bogus new `_TokenType` instance rather than raising `AttributeError`. `copy` would then try to call that non-callable `_TokenType` object as if it were a `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce_ex__` method, producing `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable` — exactly the reported failure for 'copy issue672'.

Fix applied: restored the guard clause in `__getattr__` to raise `AttributeError` for any name that starts and ends with `__`, before creating a new token type:

```python
def __getattr__(self, name):
    # don't mess with dunder
    if name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'):
        raise AttributeError
    new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
    setattr(self, name, new)
    new.parent = self
    return new
```

Verified with a script that:
- `copy.deepcopy()` on a parsed `sqlparse` statement now succeeds without error.
- `copy.deepcopy()` on a `Token` type (e.g. `Token.Keyword`) succeeds.
- Accessing `Token.__deepcopy__` correctly raises `AttributeError` instead of fabricating a bogus token.
- Normal attribute-based token creation (e.g. `Token.Keyword`, `Text.Whitespace`) still works as before.

All checks passed (exit code 0). This restores the previously-passing 'copy issue672' behaviour without affecting other functionality.

The regression has been fixed. Root cause: in `sqlparse/tokens.py`, `_TokenType.__getattr__` was missing its guard for dunder attribute names (only the comment `# don't mess with dunder` remained, with no actual check). This meant accessing dunder methods like `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce__`/`__reduce_ex__` (which Python's `copy`/`copy.deepcopy` machinery probes for) would fall through to the normal logic and dynamically create a bogus new `_TokenType` instance rather than raising `AttributeError`. `copy` would then try to call that non-callable `_TokenType` object as if it were a `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce_ex__` method, producing `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable` — exactly the reported failure for 'copy issue672'.

Fix applied: restored the guard clause in `__getattr__` to raise `AttributeError` for any name that starts and ends with `__`, before creating a new token type:

```python
def __getattr__(self, name):
    # don't mess with dunder
    if name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'):
        raise AttributeError
    new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
    setattr(self, name, new)
    new.parent = self
    return new
```

The regression has been fixed. Root cause: in `sqlparse/tokens.py`, `_TokenType.__getattr__` was missing its guard for dunder attribute names (only the comment `# don't mess with dunder` remained, with no actual check). This meant accessing dunder methods like `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce__`/`__reduce_ex__` (which Python's `copy`/`copy.deepcopy` machinery probes for) would fall through to the normal logic and dynamically create a bogus new `_TokenType` instance rather than raising `AttributeError`. `copy` would then try to call that non-callable `_TokenType` object as if it were a `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce_ex__` method, producing `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable` — exactly the reported failure for 'copy issue672'.

Fix applied: restored the guard clause in `__getattr__` to raise `AttributeError` for any name that starts and ends with `__`, before creating a new token type:

```python
def __getattr__(self, name):
    # don't mess with dunder
    if name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'):
        raise AttributeError
    new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
    setattr(self, name, new)
    new.parent = self
    return new
```

Verified with a script that:
- `copy.deepcopy()` on a parsed `sqlparse` statement now succeeds without error.
- `copy.deepcopy()` on a `Token` type (e.g. `Token.Keyword`) succeeds.
- Accessing `Token.__deepcopy__` correctly raises `AttributeError` instead of fabricating a bogus token.
- Normal attribute-based token creation (e.g. `Token.Keyword`, `Text.Whitespace`) still works as before.

All checks passed (exit code 0). This restores the previously-passing 'copy issue672' behaviour without affecting other functionality.

The regression has been fixed. Root cause: in `sqlparse/tokens.py`, `_TokenType.__getattr__` was missing its guard for dunder attribute names (only the comment `# don't mess with dunder` remained, with no actual check). This meant accessing dunder methods like `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce__`/`__reduce_ex__` (which Python's `copy`/`copy.deepcopy` machinery probes for) would fall through to the normal logic and dynamically create a bogus new `_TokenType` instance rather than raising `AttributeError`. `copy` would then try to call that non-callable `_TokenType` object as if it were a `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce_ex__` method, producing `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable` — exactly the reported failure for 'copy issue672'.

Fix applied: restored the guard clause in `__getattr__` to raise `AttributeError` for any name that starts and ends with `__`, before creating a new token type:

```python
def __getattr__(self, name):
    # don't mess with dunder
    if name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'):
        raise AttributeError
    new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
    setattr(self, name, new)
    new.parent = self
    return new
```

- `copy.deepcopy()` on a `Token` type (e.g. `Token.Keyword`) succeeds.
- Accessing `Token.__deepcopy__` correctly raises `AttributeError` instead of fabricating a bogus token.
- Normal attribute-based token creation (e.g. `Token.Keyword`, `Text.Whitespace`) still works as before.

The regression has been fixed. Root cause: in `sqlparse/tokens.py`, `_TokenType.__getattr__` was missing its guard for dunder attribute names (only the comment `# don't mess with dunder` remained, with no actual check). This meant accessing dunder methods like `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce__`/`__reduce_ex__` (which Python's `copy`/`copy.deepcopy` machinery probes for) would fall through to the normal logic and dynamically create a bogus new `_TokenType` instance rather than raising `AttributeError`. `copy` would then try to call that non-callable `_TokenType` object as if it were a `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce_ex__` method, producing `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable` — exactly the reported failure for 'copy issue672'.

Fix applied: restored the guard clause in `__getattr__` to raise `AttributeError` for any name that starts and ends with `__`, before creating a new token type:

```python
def __getattr__(self, name):
    # don't mess with dunder
    if name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'):
        raise AttributeError
    new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
    setattr(self, name, new)
    new.parent = self
    return new
```

- `copy.deepcopy()` on a parsed `sqlparse` statement now succeeds without error.
- `copy.deepcopy()` on a `Token` type (e.g. `Token.Keyword`) succeeds.
- Accessing `Token.__deepcopy__` correctly raises `AttributeError` instead of fabricating a bogus token.
- Normal attribute-based token creation (e.g. `Token.Keyword`, `Text.Whitespace`) still works as before.

The root cause was found and fixed: `_TokenType.__getattr__` in sqlparse/tokens.py was missing its dunder-attribute guard (only a comment remained), so accessing dunder methods like `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce__` (used internally by `copy.deepcopy`) would create a bogus new `_TokenType` token instead of raising `AttributeError`. When `copy` then tried to call that non-callable token object, it raised `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable`. I restored the guard clause that raises `AttributeError` for dunder names so `copy`/`deepcopy` work correctly again, while normal attribute access (e.g. `Token.Keyword`) still functions.

Let me verify with a quick script that copy.deepcopy works now and run any existing test suite that can be found.

import sqlparse
from sqlparse import tokens as T

# Basic sanity: attribute creation still works
assert T.Token.Keyword is T.Keyword

# The reported regression: copying tokens/statements should not raise TypeError
stmt = sqlparse.parse('SELECT * FROM foo')[0]
copied = copy.deepcopy(stmt)
print('deepcopy of statement OK:', copied)

copied_type = copy.deepcopy(T.Keyword)
print('deepcopy of token type OK:', copied_type)

# dunder should raise AttributeError, not create a bogus token
try:
    T.Token.__deepcopy__
    print('ERROR: expected AttributeError for __deepcopy__')
except AttributeError:
    print('AttributeError correctly raised for __deepcopy__ access')

print('ALL CHECKS PASSED')
"}

verify_issue672.py

The regression has been fixed. Root cause: in `sqlparse/tokens.py`, `_TokenType.__getattr__` was missing its guard for dunder attribute names (only the comment `# don't mess with dunder` remained, with no actual check). This meant accessing dunder methods like `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce__`/`__reduce_ex__` (which Python's `copy`/`copy.deepcopy` machinery probes for) would fall through to the normal logic and dynamically create a bogus new `_TokenType` instance rather than raising `AttributeError`. `copy` would then try to call that non-callable `_TokenType` object as if it were a `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce_ex__` method, producing `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable` — exactly the reported failure for 'copy issue672'.

Fix applied: restored the guard clause in `__getattr__` to raise `AttributeError` for any name that starts and ends with `__`, before creating a new token type:

```python
def __getattr__(self, name):
    # don't mess with dunder
    if name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'):
        raise AttributeError
    new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
    setattr(self, name, new)
    new.parent = self
    return new
```

Verified with a script that:
- `copy.deepcopy()` on a parsed `sqlparse` statement now succeeds without error.
- `copy.deepcopy()` on a `Token` type (e.g. `Token.Keyword`) succeeds.
- Accessing `Token.__deepcopy__` correctly raises `AttributeError` instead of fabricating a bogus token.
- Normal attribute-based token creation (e.g. `Token.Keyword`, `Text.Whitespace`) still works as before.

All checks passed (exit code 0). This restores the previously-passing 'copy issue672' behaviour without affecting other functionality.

The regression has been fixed. Root cause: in `sqlparse/tokens.py`, `_TokenType.__getattr__` was missing its guard for dunder attribute names (only the comment `# don't mess with dunder` remained, with no actual check). This meant accessing dunder methods like `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce__`/`__reduce_ex__` (which Python's `copy`/`copy.deepcopy` machinery probes for) would fall through to the normal logic and dynamically create a bogus new `_TokenType` instance rather than raising `AttributeError`. `copy` would then try to call that non-callable `_TokenType` object as if it were a `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce_ex__` method, producing `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable` — exactly the reported failure for 'copy issue672'.

Fix applied: restored the guard clause in `__getattr__` to raise `AttributeError` for any name that starts and ends with `__`, before creating a new token type:

```python
def __getattr__(self, name):
    # don't mess with dunder
    if name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'):
        raise AttributeError
    new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
    setattr(self, name, new)
    new.parent = self
    return new
```

- Normal attribute-based token creation (e.g. `Token.Keyword`, `Text.Whitespace`) still works as before.

The regression has been fixed. Root cause: in `sqlparse/tokens.py`, `_TokenType.__getattr__` was missing its guard for dunder attribute names (only the comment `# don't mess with dunder` remained, with no actual check). This meant accessing dunder methods like `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce__`/`__reduce_ex__` (which Python's `copy`/`copy.deepcopy` machinery probes for) would fall through to the normal logic and dynamically create a bogus new `_TokenType` instance rather than raising `AttributeError`. `copy` would then try to call that non-callable `_TokenType` object as if it were a `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce_ex__` method, producing `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable` — exactly the reported failure for 'copy issue672'.

Fix applied: restored the guard clause in `__getattr__` to raise `AttributeError` for any name that starts and ends with `__`, before creating a new token type:

```python
def __getattr__(self, name):
    # don't mess with dunder
    if name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'):
        raise AttributeError
    new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
    setattr(self, name, new)
    new.parent = self
    return new
```

Verified with a script that:
- `copy.deepcopy()` on a parsed `sqlparse` statement now succeeds without error.
- `copy.deepcopy()` on a `Token` type (e.g. `Token.Keyword`) succeeds.
- Accessing `Token.__deepcopy__` correctly raises `AttributeError` instead of fabricating a bogus token.
- Normal attribute-based token creation (e.g. `Token.Keyword`, `Text.Whitespace`) still works as before.

All checks passed (exit code 0). This restores the previously-passing 'copy issue672' behaviour without affecting other functionality.

arguments.summary:
Fixed the 'copy issue672' regression in sqlparse.

Root cause: sqlparse/tokens.py's `_TokenType.__getattr__` was missing its dunder-name guard clause (only the comment `# don't mess with dunder` remained, with no actual check). This meant accessing dunder methods like `__deepcopy__`/`__reduce_ex__` (which Python's `copy`/`copy.deepcopy` machinery probes for) fell through to the normal logic and fabricated a bogus new `_TokenType` instance instead of raising `AttributeError`. `copy` then tried to call that non-callable `_TokenType` object as if it were a method, producing `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable`.

Reproduction: I temporarily reverted the guard, ran `python repro_issue672.py` (calls `copy.deepcopy` on a parsed sqlparse statement), and confirmed it failed with exactly the reported traceback ending in `TypeError: '_TokenType' object is not callable`. I then reapplied the fix and re-ran the same script, confirming it now succeeds (exit code 0, prints the deep-copied statement).

Fix applied in sqlparse/tokens.py:

    def __getattr__(self, name):
        # don't mess with dunder
        if name.startswith('__') and name.endswith('__'):
            raise AttributeError
        new = _TokenType(self + (name,))
        setattr(self, name, new)
        new.parent = self
        return new

This also verified that normal attribute-based token creation (e.g. `Token.Keyword`, `Text.Whitespace`) still works as before, since only dunder names are now excluded. All temporary repro/verification scripts were removed afterward; the workspace contains only the one-line-added fix to sqlparse/tokens.py.
